findings.text: Serial core provides tiny inline locking helpers that couple the port spinlock with the nonblocking console bookkeeping. Taking the lock always pairs spin acquisition with console acquisition, and releasing always pairs console release with spin release, with variants preserving interrupt state.

Serial core provides a release helper that optionally drains a pending system request. When that feature is present the helper snapshots and clears the stored character under protection, drops the lock, then dispatches the snapshot outside the lock; otherwise it only drops the lock.

Reception DMA completion runs under the port interrupt lock from residue sampling through retrigger decision, and leaves through the system request aware release so a deferred console request is handled after unlocking.

The main interrupt entry holds the port lock across status sampling and dispatch, while the programmed IO receive path explicitly releases the lock around delivery to the line discipline and any attempt to resume DMA, then reacquires before returning.

Short control updates use interrupt safe acquisition only around register and flag mutation, covering poll timeout demotion, shutdown DMA disable, receive throttling, break programming and both RS485 timer handlers.

Half duplex transmit gating moves through idle, sending and timed waits after asserting request to send and after completing transmission. Entry programs transmitter, receiver and request lines from port flags, optionally arms a start delay timer, and timer expirations advance the machine or cancel the peer timer.

Receive DMA alternates between two buffers with a running flag and an active selector. Interrupt, completion and timer events harvest arrived bytes, flip the selector, and immediately arm the next transfer; any arming failure clears running and unmasks receive interrupts so programmed IO continues.

Starting a receive DMA job requires a DMA channel and a preparable descriptor. Missing channel reports an IO failure, preparation failure stops the running indication, halts the channel and reports busy to request interrupt fallback, while success enables DMA reception, suppresses receive interrupts and marks running with a completion callback armed.

Receive harvesting prefers DMA bytes before FIFO bytes. Accepted bytes enter the TTY flip buffer and advance the receive counter, short insertion warns about a full discipline, error flags are cleared before any FIFO drain, FIFO drain occurs only when DMA is fully consumed and explicitly allowed, and every harvest ends with a push.

Both polled and event driven paths derive newly arrived counts from DMA residue against buffer length and a cached residue value, adjusting for bytes already consumed by polling and bounding the result to the DMA buffer capacity.

DMA startup proceeds only if probed channels exist, allocating transmit storage and both receive buffers, switching the visible FIFO capacity to DMA size, enabling error response and vendor thresholds, then attempting an initial receive job and optional polling timer. Shutdown waits for controller idle, disables DMA enables under lock, synchronously halts channels, releases mappings and storage, stops timers and clears usage flags.

Builds without DMA engine support degenerate cleanly to programmed IO. Receive trigger reports IO failure, availability and running predicates stay false, transmit DMA start declines, receive interrupt handling and stop plus startup plus shutdown plus removal do nothing, and the flush hook is absent.

The device interrupt entry samples masked status, acknowledges everything except transmit and receive indications, routes receive timeouts to DMA or programmed IO handling, routes modem changes and transmit empty to their handlers, repeats while status persists up to a pass bound, then releases with system request processing and reports whether anything was handled.

Asynchronous receive progress arrives through several entries: a polling timer that incrementally forwards newly arrived DMA bytes and demotes to interrupts after idle timeout, and two high resolution timers plus a DMA completion callback that advance RS485 timing and buffer turnover.

Upper layer operations gate transmission through RS485 state and DMA-or-programmed choice, halt reception by masking receive and error interrupts plus stopping DMA, throttle by halting under lock, enable modem interrupts, and program modem outputs and break from abstract control values.

Observed driver state groups a transmit side with channel, linear buffer, length, mapping and queued flag, a receive side with channel, two DMA buffers, active selector, running flag, transfer cookie, poll rate and timeout plus timer and residue timestamps, and port extensions for cached control and mask values, usage flags, probe flag, FIFO size, vendor quirks, RS485 state with timers, and last modem status.

Oversized DMA counts trap as programming errors, incomplete TTY insertion only warns and may drop bytes, DMA pause failures only log while proceeding, shutdown spins on a busy flag, interrupt looping is bounded to avoid livelock, and receive stop currently only clears the enable without halting the channel.

Modem evaluation reads combined status, compares against cached value to find edges, notifies data carrier and clear to send transitions, counts data set ready edges, wakes modem waiters, and when a vendor quirk is flagged clears interrupts with dummy reads to enforce ordering.

Modem input mapping converts controller status bits including vendor specific positions into abstract carrier, data set, clear and ring indications. Output mapping converts abstract request, data terminal, auxiliary and loopback indications into control bits, coupling automatic request handling to the requested level.
Break assertion uses control value negative one; any other value clears break.
